title: Wes Montgomery and Tanglewood with Getz

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I heard an interesting story about Wes Montgomery. When Wes made his recordings in the sixties with Don Sebesky, it got to a point that Wes-- apparentlyonce they got him in the studio they tried to do the recording there with string players and woodwind players, and he was just so intimidated by the whole process they eventually just had him come in with the rhythm section and laid down his tracks, and then Sebesky would write the padding around it.
No, it couldn't be if they were writing around.
Unless what they did was Sebesky took over (inaudible).
I guess there's more than one side to a problem like that.
Maybe he was reacting the same way I was reacting. I know that happened with Stan-- although he doesn't admit it--up in Tanglewood. He asked me to write a piece for him--did we discuss this?
There's this huge hall and you get overwhelmed by this and I wrote a (inaudible). Everything fell down and he was reading off the floor at one point.
In that case, did they make--this was for the Boston Pops;
